subject.title: build(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Are the reviewed upstream action SHAs, especially Codex Action 1.11 and the token/login/release action updates, approved to execute in OpenClaw's credentialed and security-sensitive workflows?
rationale: These pins replace executable third-party bundles in privileged workflows, and repository policy assigns several touched paths to security owners while requiring direct Codex runtime-contract inspection.

options.title: Approve after contract check
options.body: Complete direct Codex source inspection and fresh required checks, then approve the grouped pin update if no privilege or compatibility change is found.

options.title: Split the sensitive pins
options.body: Land routine setup actions separately and move Codex, token, login, release, and CodeQL pins into smaller security-reviewed PRs.

options.title: Keep current pins
options.body: Close or defer the grouped update if security owners cannot validate the new executable bundles and workflow contracts.

recommendation.title: Approve after contract check
recommendation.body: Complete direct Codex source inspection and fresh required checks, then approve the grouped pin update if no privilege or compatibility change is found.

likelyOwner.reason: Workflow history makes steipete the strongest individual routing candidate, while CODEOWNERS separately requires the security-operations team on the sensitive paths.
